text: The aim of damages is to restore the claimant to the position that he or she would have been in if
the tort had not occurred.
Explain the types of damages available in a claim for negligence. Assess the extent to which the
aim above can be achieved. [25]
Explain the rules relating to remoteness of damage in negligence. Assess whether the current
rules achieve justice for the parties. [25]
‘The responsibility for the safety of little children must rest primarily upon the parents…’
Lord Devlin. Phipps v Rochester Corporation [1955]
Explain the legal duty owed by an occupier towards a child visitor. Assess the validity of the
statement above. [25]
Section B
Jane is looking for a large commercial property to purchase for use as office space for
40 employees. She sees an advertisement for an auction to be held by AB Property (ABP). She
looks at ABP’s website and then visits its office to discuss her requirements.
Brian, ABP’s senior auctioneer, recommends a particular property and provides Jane with a written
document which contains full details of its dimensions. He had relied on measurements given by
the current owner when compiling the document.
Jane attends the auction and purchases the property without viewing it. When she goes to the
property, she finds that it is 30% smaller than stated in the document provided by ABP and
therefore not big enough to accommodate her business.
Advise Jane, Brian and ABP as to their rights and responsibilities in negligence arising from this
situation. [25]
Helen has operated a helicopter hire business from a small airfield for the last 10 years. Two years
ago, Denis purchased a house close to the airfield.
In the last six months, Helen’s business has grown. The hours of operation were 10:00 to 16:00
Monday to Friday. The business now operates 08:00 to 20:00 every day. The number of helicopters
in use has increased from three to six.
Denis has complained to Helen on a number of occasions about the noise and vibrations of the
helicopters throughout the day and evening. As Denis works from home he is finding the noise
very disruptive. He is also concerned about the strong smell of aviation fuel and feels unable to
continue growing vegetables in his garden due to the risk of soil contamination.
Advise Denis as to his rights and remedies in relation to private nuisance in this situation. [25]
Charles takes his 10‑year‑old son, Harry, to Thrillseekers theme park. The park has recently
opened a new ride and advertises it as the biggest of its kind and restricted to riders aged 12 and
over.
When they are getting on the ride, the operator, William, asks Harry’s age. Charles says that Harry
is 12 years old. William allows them on the ride but does not check that the safety harnesses have
been secured once they are seated.
During the ride, Harry’s harness suddenly opens and he is thrown to the ground. He sustains
serious injuries. Jane, a nurse, also visiting the park, rushes to assist and treats Harry until the
ambulance arrives. Charles calls his wife, Fiona, as he accompanies Harry in the ambulance,
telling her that their son is badly injured. Fiona arrives just as Harry is brought in to the hospital.
Jane is severely traumatised by the incident and is unable to work. Harry has to be treated in
hospital for several months and Fiona has been diagnosed with depression.
Advise the parties as to their rights and responsibilities in negligence. [25]
